title: Apple Says Former Engineer Used Stolen Trade Secrets at OpenAI, Taught AI Agent to Run Them
content:
Apple today submitted new evidence in its lawsuit against OpenAI, with the hope that the new information will persuade the judge to grant an expedited discovery process.


Apple filed a theft of trade secrets lawsuit against OpenAI employees Chang Liu and Tang Tan in July, accusing them of using multiple methods to steal data from Apple. Liu kept an Apple-issued MacBook after he left for OpenAI, and Apple got it back after the lawsuit was filed. Apple now says forensic analysis of the laptop has uncovered more evidence of Liu's use of Apple information and his attempts to hide what he'd done.

From the lawsuit:

 	
Mr. Liu not only downloaded a confidential Apple circuit schematic but also used it in his work at OpenAI;

 	
Far from his unauthorized access to Apple's third-party cloud storage being unknown to him, Mr. Liu and others at OpenAI were well-aware of that access;

 	
Mr. Liu, upon learning of Apple's internal investigation of him, sent instructions for destroying evidence to an OpenAI colleague who confirmed she would comply; and

 	
Mr. Liu used a tool in his work at OpenAI that has the same name as an internal Apple engineering application used for Apple development work.


Liu downloaded the circuit schematic from Apple in March, two months after he left the company. Liu used the schematic to run a simulation using electrical engineering tool LTspice, and then messaged people telling them he ran the simulation for power conversion development work. Liu described how he trained an AI agent to run LTspice.

According to the filing, he said he was "[f]eeling AI all day long," and that "[i]n the past hour," his AI "agent learned how to run LTspice, look at result, tune compensation parameter." "I try to make a behavior buck," he wrote. "With voltage outer and current inner. Everything ideal. It still took me a day.. now it's two hour. Including learning fresh."

"Oh man! Why do they even need you then?" the person Liu was talking to reportedly replied.

Mac mini that later synced to the MacBook he took from Apple, which is why Apple knows about it. Apple now wants to investigate the ‌Mac mini‌ and other devices Liu still has in his possession.

Apple says the "shocking evidence" is proof that its trade secrets are in active use and evidence is being destroyed, which is why expedited discovery is needed.

dismiss the lawsuit, claiming the accusations were "meritless." OpenAI also published a public statement calling the lawsuit "careless, aggressive and oddly personal" and stating that it does not "have, nor want, any of their trade secrets" because it is "much more interested in building innovative products and technologies that push the frontier."

title: Apple ninja edits Mac Studio specs to remove PCIe Gen 6 storage reference
content:
Macworld





During Apple surprise Mac announcements last week, the company declared in its press release that the Mac Studio features “a next-generation SSD architecture built on PCIe Gen 6.” However, that mention has since been removed from the Mac Studio press release and site, as spotted by MacGeneration. 
The PCIe Gen 6 statement has been removed from the Apple U.K., Apple Germany, and Apple Japan press releases, though strangely, the PCIe Gen 6 reference still exists in the Apple France press release. The releases still list August 25, 2026, as the day of publication and have no record of an update, but we, along with many other outlets, quoted the PCIe Gen 6 in our original stories and haven’t been contacted by Apple about a correction.
The press release now reads, “Storage performance is up to twice as fast, with a next-generation SSD architecture, delivering industry-leading read and write speeds for rapid project loading, file transfers, and loading huge LLMs.” The twice as fast comparision is to the M3 Ultra Mac Studio.
The Internet Archive has a copy of the U.S. Mac Studio press release, recorded on August 25 at 13:03:29, and it contains the PCIe Gen 6 reference. Other copies recorded by the Internet Archive on August 25 still have the reference, but the first record of the press release on August 26 at 02:03:13 shows that the release was revised to remove references to PCIe Gen 6.
PCIe Gen 6 is the next generation of the PCIe interconnect standard, offering performance upgrades over the PCIe Gen 5 standard. Apple did not specify that the M5 Ultra Mac Studio implements PCIe Gen 5, but the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips are equipped with it. So it’s likely that the M5 Ultra has it too, and Apple made an error in its press release.
Apple was contacted for clarification and had yet to respond at the time of this posting.
creator: Macworld

title: Apple Adds Three More Macs to Obsolete Products List
content:
Apple today added three Macs to its list of obsolete products. The 2018 Retina MacBook Air, the 13-inch 2018 MacBook Pro with four Thunderbolt 3 ports, and the 13-inch 2017 ‌MacBook Pro‌ with two Thunderbolt 3 ports are now considered obsolete.


The three products were previously part of the vintage list, but have been moved. Apple adds a product to the vintage list when it's been five years since it was last distributed for sale, and it becomes obsolete at the seven-year mark.

Vintage products can still be repaired at Apple retail locations and by Apple Authorized Service Providers if Apple has the parts available. Devices that are obsolete are generally not eligible for repair, and Apple stops making repair components.

Apple has a battery-only repair policy for Mac laptops for up to 10 years after the Mac was last distributed for sale, so 2017/2018 ‌MacBook Pro‌ and 2018 ‌MacBook Air‌ owners may still be able to get battery replacements.

Touch ID and a Retina display. Prior ‌MacBook Air‌ models had a non-Retina display with much lower resolution and less vibrant colors. 2018 was also a redesign year for the ‌MacBook Air‌, with Apple introducing smaller bezels and a thinner, lighter chassis.

title: Longtime exec Phil Schiller is downgrading his role at Apple again
content:
Macworld





Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reported on Monday that Apple executive Phil Schiller is stepping down from his roles as leader of the App Store and manager of product events. The news comes on Tim Cook’s last day as Apple CEO.
Schiller became an Apple Fellow in 2020 after initially stepping down as SVP of Worldwide Marketing, a position he had held since 2000. He joined Apple as a product marketing manager in 1987, but left in 1995 for Macromedia. He rejoined Apple in 1997 when Steve Jobs returned to the company.
When Schiller became an Apple Fellow, he relinquished his marketing role to Greg Joswiak, but he continued to lead the efforts for the App Store and product events. The App Store duties move over to Apple’s services division, which is run by SVP Eddy Cue. Carson Oliver will run the App Store on a daily basis.
Apple’s events team is now run by Nola Weinstein, who has acted as “Schiller’s deputy since 2023,” according to Gurman. Weinstein reports to Kristin Huguet Quayle, Apple’s vice president of communications and public relations.
Schiller will still serve as an Apple Fellow and will work “on unspecified initiatives,” but the change is an indication that Schiller is moving towards full retirement. When he stepped down as SVP in 2020, it was viewed as the start of a gradual move towards leaving the company.
Apple’s executive suite has been undergoing a series of personal changes in the past few years as leaders age towards retirement. Lisa Jackson (VP for Environment, Policy, and Social Initiatives) retired in January, John Giannandrea (SVP, Machine Learning and AI) retired in April, and Katherine Adams (SVP Government Affairs) will retire by the end of the year. In 2025, Luca Maestri (CFO) and Jeff Williams (COO) retired, whille Alan Dye (VP Human Interface Design) left for Meta. And of course, Tim Cook steps down as CEO this week.
The executive changes will be a challenge for incoming CEO John Ternus, but the company is in a position where it is seeing growth and success with all of its products. At the same time, Apple clearly needs to show it can develop and incorporate AI-based technologies to show progress going forward. New blood can help drive Apple towards that goal.

title: Apple Seemingly Made a Mistake When Announcing the New Mac Studio
content:
Apple's press release for the new Mac Studio with M5 Max and M5 Ultra chips last week initially stated that the computer had "next-generation SSD architecture built on PCIe Gen 6." However, as spotted by the French blog MacGeneration, Apple removed the PCIe 6.0 mention from the announcement shortly after it was published.


The press release still mentions that the new Mac Studio has a "next-generation SSD architecture" that delivers up to twice as fast storage speeds compared to the previous generation, but it no longer mentions PCIe 6.0. Apple has yet to respond to our request for comment, but it seems like the company simply made a mistake in the press release, as it is much more likely that the new Mac Studio supports the PCIe 5.0 standard.

First, we already know that the 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pro models with the same M5 Max chip available in the new Mac Studio have SSDs with PCIe 5.0, and Apple likewise advertised up to twice as fast SSD speeds for those laptops. Second, there are no consumer PCs on the market yet that have SSDs with PCIe 6.0 support.

The M5 Ultra chip is all new, but it probably supports PCIe 5.0 as well, or else Apple would not have needed to edit its Mac Studio press release.

title: iOS 27 beta 8 is out now as the general release date approaches
content:
Macworld





On the first day of the WWDC developer conference, Apple released the first developer beta of its new operating system. This year, that means that the first release of iOS 27 outside Cupertino came on June 8, 2026.
The pattern goes like this: Apple releases developer-only betas for the first month or so, and then starts releasing the same build for both developers and public beta testers. With only a month or less before the general release, most of the beta updates now are minor in scope, focused on polish, optimization, and fixing the last bugs.
If you want to try out the new OS 27 updates and provide feedback, check out our article on how to become a beta tester. It’s easy.
Updated August 31, 2026: The eighth beta of iOS 27 is now available to developers, and should be released to the public testers within the next day or so. We’re just a week or two away from the final wide release.
What’s new in iOS 27
The big iOS 27 release this year is focused on three main areas:
Trust and Safety – New parental controls to keep kids safe and control screen time.
Performance and refinement – Speeding everything up, improving efficiency, tweaking interfaces, and addressing dozens of small user requests.
Apple Intelligence and Siri – Entirely new Apple Intelligence models improve AI throughout the system, and a brand-new Siri is vastly more capable than ever before.
For a more complete breakdown of all the new features and changes, check out our iOS 27 guide.
With just a week or two before the final wide release, the betas are focused on fixing bugs, security flaws, and performance and not on making big visible changes.
iOS 27: How to install the developer beta
You’ll need to be registered as an Apple Developer, but a free developer account will do. You can get one via Xcode or the Apple Developer app in iOS. Here’s how to do it via the Apple Developer app:
Download the Apple Developer App from the App Store.
Open the app.
Tap on Account.
Sign in using your usual Apple ID.
Once you have a free developer account, just follow the same instructions as with the public beta:
Open Settings.
Tap General, then Software Update.
Make sure the Beta Updates selection is set to iOS 27 Developer Beta.
Follow the on-screen instructions.
iOS 27: How to install the public beta
The first iOS 27 public beta is not available yet but is expected to arrive in July. When it lands, you can follow these steps to test it out even if you’re not a developer:
Click Sign Up on the Apple Beta page and register with your Apple ID.
Log in to the Beta Software Program.
Click Enroll your iOS device.
Open the Settings app, tap General, then Software Update.
In the Beta Updates section, select the iOS 27 Public Beta.
It may take a few moments after registering for the beta option to appear in Software Update. 
If you want to uninstall the iOS 27 beta read: How to remove an iOS beta from your iPhone.

Visual Intelligence is now on the Mac so ‌Siri‌ can answer questions about what's on your screen, and a Write with ‌Siri‌ feature lets ‌Siri‌ generate text or give feedback on your writing.

title: The original Mac gets a starring role in ‘Mayday’ Apple TV promo
content:
Macworld





A large number of Macworld readers have been using the Mac for a long time. But even if you weren’t using the first Mac that Apple released in 1984, we all know how revolutionary those early years of the Mac were.
But let’s be honest. 1980s tech relied on floppy disks, and the newest promo for the Apple TV movie Mayday reminds us all how much that sucked. Mayday is set during the 1980s, and in the promo, Mayday stars Ryan Reynolds and Kenneth Branagh decide to demo the film using what looks like an original Macintosh.


Not only is he a master thespian who has performed the greatest works of the Bard, Kenneth Branagh is a certified Mac Genius Support specialist. Mayday on @AppleTV September 4. pic.twitter.com/9FX23lls1H
— Ryan Reynolds (@VancityReynolds) August 31, 2026





As bitmapped animations play, the Mac crashes–the sad Mac tone is a nice touch. Branagh pulls out the tool every Certified Apple Technician had with them at all times: a paper clip, but just any paper clip, though, an “authentic 80s paper clip.” If you’re not familiar, a paper clip could be inserted in a small hole next to the floppy drive to manually eject a disk. It really was a vital tool.
The promo ends by reminding us all of the nightmare that epitomized the floppy disk era: the dreaded floppy disk shuffle. Reynolds reaction was exactly that of Mac users everywhere in the 1980s. 
Mayday set during the 1980s Cold War, is about an American Navy pilot (Reynolds) who crash-lands in the Soviet Union. He meets an ex-KGB agent (Branagh), and hijinks ensue. It’s not clear if the Mac plays a role in the movie, but you can find out this Friday, September 4, when the movie lands on Apple TV.

title: Apple Watch Series 12 (2026): Everything we know so far
content:
Macworld





If you’re thinking about buying an Apple Watch, you’ll want to know whether or not Apple is likely to launch a new model in the near future. After all, there are few things worse than spending hundreds of dollars on a tech device only to see it superseded by something better (and potentially cheaper) a couple of months later. Macworld is here to help you avoid that nightmare scenario.
At the time of writing, Apple sells three smartwatches: the SE 3, the Series 11, and the Ultra 3. All three were announced in September last year, which means we’re expecting at least one to be updated in the next few months. 
In this article we’ve gathered all the information currently available about the new Apple Watch(es) coming in 2026. This includes rumors about the likely release date, changes to the design, the tech specs and features of the new models, and their expected pricing.
For detailed comparison of Apple’s smartwatches, check out our giant guide to the best Apple Watch in 2026.
Apple Watch Series 12 release date: Will Apple release a new Apple Watch soon?
The next Apple Watch will launch on September 9
Apple products can be divided into two categories: Those that get a new model every year like clockwork (the iPhone and the Apple Watch), and those that don’t (everything else). In other words, yes, Apple is going to release a new watch soon.
Every September since 2016, the company has announced a new “Series” brand Apple Watch. The schedule is so regular that you can set your smartwatch by it. So the Series 12 will almost certainly make its first appearance at a special press event in September 2026, alongside the iPhone 18 Pro, which will be held on September 9.
What about the Apple Watch SE 4 and Ultra 4?
The latest rumors say we will be getting an Ultra 4 but will have to wait at last another year for a new SE.
The SE and Ultra sub-brands are less predictable, unfortunately, than the Series models. Yes, the SE 3 and Ultra 3 were both announced on September 9, 2025. But new models don’t come out every year. The schedule is less regular:
SE 1: September 2020
SE 2: September 2022
SE 3: September 2025
Ultra 1: September 2022
Ultra 2: September 2023
Ultra 3: September 2025




Apple Watch Series 12 design: Is the new Apple Watch getting a redesign?
A major redesign appears unlikely
Ceramic option could return
Last summer, a report from DigiTimes raised hopes that 2026 would see the Apple Watch get its first major redesign. But such rumors come up fairly regularly (there was lots of talk about a flat Apple Watch Series X around the time of the Series 7), and so far none of them have materialised.
Indeed, three months later, the Weibo poster Instant Digital insisted that neither the Series 12 nor the Series 13 would get a new look, and that the big redesign was actually coming in 2028. This is how it tends to go: pundits and leakers get publicity from predicting Apple Watch redesigns, and then Apple ends up sticking to essentially the same design because it dominates the market and doesn’t need to take any risks.
Based on this, and the fact that nobody has leaked any radical new CAD drawings or photos of a redesigned chassis from the supply chain, we’d cautiously predict that (aside, potentially, from a slightly larger screen, fractionally slimmer bezels, or a new color), the Apple Watch is going to stay essentially the same for yet another year. But for the sake of variety, we’d love to be wrong about that.
However, a report from Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman claims that Apple has tested a white and dark gray ceramic model that could make an appearance this year. The last time Apple sold a ceramic watch was the Edition model in 2019.

				
					

				
			Apple Watches have looked roughly the same for years.
David Price / Foundry




Apple Watch Series 12 specs and features: Will the new Apple Watch get a major upgrade?
Faster S12 processor
Same battery life
Continuous heart-rate tracking
Whereas design tends to stay largely the same from year to year, as discussed above, Apple habitually makes worthwhile upgrades to the Apple Watch’s internals.
S12 processor
Let’s start with the processor, and this is one pattern that changed last year. Every Apple Watch from Series 1 to 10 had a corresponding chip, from the S1 to the S10. But the Series 11 came with… the S10 again. Even the Ultra 3 was stuck with the previous year’s chip.
It’s unlikely that Apple will freeze the processor for another year, so we’d expect the Series 12 to get something new. Whether that will be an S11 (logical) or S12 (neater, since it matches the Series number, plus it sounds newer and therefore better) doesn’t really matter to customers, since the labels are more of a marketing tool than anything else. The real-world performance upgrade varies widely from generation to generation; in fact, the S6, S7, and S8 were essentially identical.
Our expectation would be an S12 processor with a moderate performance bump from the S10. But processing speed isn’t much of a bottleneck for the Apple Watch anyway, so we should be looking elsewhere for more meaningful change.
Continuous heart-rate monitoring
A report in August from Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman claimed that Apple has been testing a feature that will allow the Apple watch to ““continuously collect data throughout the day” through the heart-rate sensor. Currently, it collects sporadic readings when not in the Heart Rate, Mindfulness, or Workout apps.
microLED screen
Perhaps the screen will get an upgrade? The Apple Watch has always had an OLED screen, and the past three Series models have been capped at 2,000 nits of brightness. (The Ultra 3 can go up to 3,000.) But there have been rumours for some years, dating back to the Apple Watch X theories, that Apple would like to switch to superior microLED tech.
microLED means improved color fidelity and better power efficiency. But the biggest impact could be on brightness. At CES in 2025, Samsung showed off a concept capable of 4,000 nits. There’s a good chance this is coming at some point, but it may not happen in 2026.

				
					

				
			The Series 11 has an always-on screen, but it leaves something to be desired on the brightness front.
David Price / Foundry




Touch ID
Another long-running rumor, but one that gained traction in late summer 2025. Apple has at the very least been exploring the idea of putting a fingerprint sensor in the Apple Watch.
Macworld has seen developer code clearly referring to the 2026 Apple Watch models and mentioning support for “AppleMesa,” Apple’s internal codename for Touch ID. No previous models have featured such mentions in their code.
At the time of discovery, this appeared to be at the prototype stage, so we can’t be sure it’s coming to actual shipping products. But Touch ID on the Apple Watch, whether hidden in a side button or beneath the screen, would be useful for Apple Pay, health/fitness apps, and private messaging, not to mention unlocking the device when its companion iPhone isn’t around.
Blood glucose tracking
Apple often gives the Apple Watch a new health or safety feature from time to time, but it’s been a few years since the last such upgrade. While the Series 8 was the first model to get crash detection, and hypertension and sleep apnea notifications were new on the Series 9, the Series 10 and 11 missed out in that department.
The Series 12 could reverse that trend with blood glucose tracking, yet another long-term rumor.
Really long term, in fact: Macworld reported on this back in 2017, when sources claimed Apple had a secret team of biomedical engineers working on non-invasive, continuous glucose monitoring to help diabetes patients, and it’s since emerged that research on this topic was underway in the Steve Jobs era.
Activity by a British medical sensing firm led to more speculation in 2021, and we understand that the feature reached the “proof of concept” in 2023. This could finally be the year, but the feature remains a long shot.
watchOS 27 and Siri AI
As the latest incarnation of Apple’s smartwatch hardware, the Series 12 will of course run the company’s latest software, which means plenty of new features that haven’t been available in the past (and won’t be available on some older Apple Watches).
watchOS 27 was announced at WWDC in June 2026 and will become publicly available in the fall. For a detailed discussion of its changes and new features, have a listen to episode 988 of the Macworld Podcast.






The biggest news on the software front, however, concerns Siri AI. The Apple Watch hasn’t previously had access to Apple’s AI tech, but that’s all changing this year.
watchOS 27 with Apple Intelligence and Siri AI requires an Apple Watch Series 9 or later, Ultra 2 or later, or SE 3. You’ll also need a compatible iPhone.
Apple Watch Series 12 price: Will the price of the Apple Watch go up this year?
We expect the Series 12 to start at around $429
On June 25, 2026, Apple announced dramatic price rises across most of its range, including iPads, Apple TVs, HomePods, and both desktop and laptop Macs. The Apple Watch escaped unscathed, which is good news, right?
Probably. It’s important to note that Apple’s statement at the time said the company had “now reached a point where we need to begin ⁠raising prices on a number of products, including today’s increases for iPad and Mac.” That suggests that there’s more to come, which may include higher starting prices for the new Apple Watch (and iPhone) models in the fall.
The main point in favor of flat pricing for the watches is their comparatively low RAM allocation. Rising RAM prices are one of the main contributors to the situation, and Apple Watches have far less RAM than iPads and Macs.
But we’d expect a small price increase compared to the Series 11, which (at time of writing!) starts at $399, or $499 for the cellular models. Around $429 seems likely.
Should you wait to buy the Apple Watch?
We think so. Now is a bad time to buy an Apple Watch at full price, and even if you can get one on sale, you should wait if you possibly can.
We’ll get new Apple Watches in September 2026: certainly the Series 12, and potentially the Ultra 4 and SE 4. These devices will have better specs and features than the current models, and should be worth waiting a few months.
While the new watches may be slightly more expensive, the existing models will still be available from third-party retailers or second hand (including Apple’s official Refurbished Stores, both U.S. and U.K.). The moment new models are announced, the asking price for the late-2025 Apple Watches will drop.

title: Tim Cook signs off as CEO with thanks to staff and a tribute to John Ternus
content:
On his last day as CEO of Apple, Tim Cook has sent a memo to every employee thanking them for what the company has achieved. Here's what he said.


Tim Cook - image credit: Apple.
Tim Cook had his going away party back on August 24, 2026, and in truth he's been steadily stepping back from his CEO role since at least April when his successor was announced. But now in his last hours leading the company, Cook has sent a heartfelt and optimistic memo to all staff.

Team,

Today is my last day as CEO of Apple. This is a moment I always knew would come one day, and yet it is still hard to believe it has arrived and I am writing these words. I love this company and the team behind it, and I couldn't let this day pass without sending a note to you, to tell you how grateful I am for the outpouring of affection you've sent my way, for the way you've shown up each and every day, and most of all, for the privilege of a lifetime serving as your leader.

The truth is, whatever there is to say about my success, I know it is all because of you. You have brought out the best in me. In all my life, I have never seen or been with such an extraordinary team of people before, and every day I get to see more examples of that.

There is something truly special about Apple. I am most proud of what an annual report could never capture. This place is proof that culture triumphs over everything. We share a belief that what we build matters, and that we have both the opportunity and the responsibility to leave the world better than we found it. That purpose is part of what makes this place extraordinary. Apple helps nurture it, but I believe it lived within each of you long before you arrived here. 

It is what brought you to this company and what continues to drive the work you do every day. Together, we have created something far greater than any one of us could have imagined or accomplished alone. And that's the secret to our success. We bring out the best in each other. We lift each other up. We have made it possible to leave our "dent in the universe," as Steve once described it, because of who we are and what we believe, because of what we value and how we see the world. How fortunate we are. How fortunate I am.

As you know, I am not leaving Apple. But I am stepping away from a role that I have loved deeply. I will miss this work in ways I can only begin to imagine, even as I remain completely at peace with my decision. I will miss leading you and being with you for every step, even as I take enormous comfort in handing the helm to someone as brilliant and wonderful and capable as John. Few people understand what it takes to build products that change the world the way John does and I could not be more excited for his leadership.

I hope you know how much I appreciate you and what an honor it has been to be your CEO. Most of all, I hope you will continue to be proud to be part of this remarkable place we call Apple and always give it your very best. When we bring our whole selves to this work, with care for one another and for the people we serve, there is no limit to the profound difference we can make.

I look forward to seeing you in my new role at Apple Park and around the world.

With all I have and all I am, I am always

Yours,

Tim

title: Apple Watch Series 12 features leaked ahead of Apple’s fall event
content:
Macworld





Apple’s Surprise and Shine iPhone event is a week from Wednesday, and while all eyes will be on the iPhone 18 Pro and folding iPhone Ultra, Apple is also expected to unveil the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4. Rumors suggest that the updates will be minor, but a new report sheds some light on what will be new this year.
In his latest Power On newsletter, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman confirms that Apple’s new Series 12 and Ultra 4 watches will be “fairly minor upgrades,” but shares some information about the new models, particularly the Series 12. Of note, he reports that there will be “many new band colors and configurations” this year, including a possible reemergence of ceramic “Edition” models (codename Iceman), which haven’t been sold since 2019. Gurman says white and dark gray options have been tested for the Series 12, but doesn’t say whether the Ultra will be getting new ceramic options as well, but due to its rugged nature, it’s unlikely.
Gurman points out the other than the new bands, Apple’s 2026 watches are unlikely to look much different than the ones released over the past several years. Instead, upgrades will once again be on the inside. He doesn’t mention whether there will be any new sensors, but he spotlights an upgrade to an existing one. Apple is reportedly testing the ability of the heart-rate sensor to “continuously collect data throughout the day.”
As it currently works, Apple’s heart-rate sensor only monitors your heart rate in real time for workouts, Breathe and Reflect sessions, and when you open the Heart Rate app. It also takes sporadic readings throughout the day to check for unusually high, low, or irregular rhythms. This new feature would allow it to work all day to get a clearer and constant picture of your health.
He also says Apple is “revamping its fitness and health app software” to better compete with screenless trackers from Whoop and Oura. As we wrote in our comparison test, Whoop has a superior app experience, which includes a journal of daily habits to personalize the fitness experience. Gurman says the refresh will “show more wellness-related metrics.”
Finally, Gurman says Apple is indeed working on “a big redesign,” as has been rumored for a while, but it’s still at least a year away.

title: Google Maps Showing 'Lake America' in U.S., Apple Maps Yet to Follow
content:
Google Maps users in the U.S. will now see the name "Lake America" instead of "Lake Ontario" for the Great Lake that straddles the New York—Ontario border.


Google said it made this change in response to the U.S. Geographic Names Information System (GNIS) updating the name for "Lake Ontario" to "Lake America," following an executive order issued by U.S. President Donald Trump last week.


Google Maps users in Canada will still see the "Lake Ontario" name only, while users outside of the U.S. and Canada will see both names.

In the U.S.: Lake America

In Canada: Lake Ontario

Outside of the U.S. and Canada: Lake Ontario (Lake America)
Apple Maps has yet to be updated, so it still shows the "Lake Ontario" name worldwide. When the GNIS updated the name for "Gulf of Mexico" to "Gulf of America" last year, Apple Maps began rolling out the change one day after Google Maps, so it might not be long before Apple follows suit with this "Lake America" change.

title: Tim Cook Steps Down as Apple CEO Tomorrow
content:
The end of an era is upon us, as Tim Cook will be stepping down as Apple's CEO on September 1, after 15 years of leading the company.

Cook has been Apple's CEO since 2011

Tomorrow, Apple's hardware engineering chief John Ternus will become the company's next CEO. Cook will remain at Apple as the executive chairman of the company's board of directors. In this new role, Apple said Cook will assist with "certain aspects" of the company, including "engaging with policymakers around the world."

Cook became Apple's CEO in August 2011, after Steve Jobs stepped down due to health problems. Under his leadership, Apple became the world's most valuable company on multiple occasions, and it launched products and services such as the Apple Watch, AirPods, HomePod, Vision Pro, Apple Music, Apple TV, and much more.  

Subscribe to the MacRumors YouTube channel for more videos.

Apple has set all-time quarterly revenue records over its past few quarters, so the company is in a strong financial position as Cook hands the reins to Ternus.

"It has been the greatest privilege of my life to be the CEO of Apple and to have been trusted to lead such an extraordinary company," said Cook. "I love Apple with all of my being, and I am so grateful to have had the opportunity to work with a team of such ingenious, innovative, creative, and deeply caring people who have been unwavering in their dedication to enriching the lives of our customers and creating the best products and services in the world."

Ternus (left) and Cook (right)

"John Ternus has the mind of an engineer, the soul of an innovator, and the heart to lead with integrity and with honor," said Cook. "He is a visionary whose contributions to Apple over 25 years are already too numerous to count, and he is without question the right person to lead Apple into the future."

title: Apple finally hits a VR home run
content:
Macworld





I’ve never had a desire to buy a Vision Pro. Even if I had $4,000 to blow at the Apple Store, I’d probably pick up a loaded MacBook Pro or a Mac mini with a Studio Display XDR instead of Apple’s cutting-edge handset.
But Friday Night Baseball in Apple Immersive changed my perspective. The first-ever broadcast of a live Major League Baseball game with 3D video recorded in 8K with a 180-degree field of view, watching the Red Sox-Yankees game on the Vision Pro was almost as breathtaking as being at Yankee Stadium. Even if I was able to take screenshots of the experience, it wouldn’t have done it justice. It’s literally the kind of thing you need to see to believe.
Most of the time I was watching the game from just beside the dugout of the team that was batting. I could turn to see the on-deck batter warming up, watch the pitch come in, and see the whole park in front of me. As usual for Apple’s Friday Night Baseball, the picture quality was outstanding, from the on-field action to the footprints and sunflower seeds in the dirt below my view. I’ve visitied many baseball stadiums and sat in all kinds of seats, but nothing compared to the immersive view Apple provided. You can get a sense of it in the post below, but a flat image doesn’t really do it justice.
While the camera put me inside the stadium, the broadcast still let me know that I was watching Apple TV. Paul Severino and Xavier Scruggs were the dedicated announcers (different from the ones on the Apple TV broadcast), and they often reminded viewers that they were witnessing something special. If I looked up, I could watch the flat Apple TV scoreboard and see relevant stats.


Live immersive MLB on Apple Vision Pro. It felt like I was at Yankee Stadium. The whole experience was incredible.
Shot through the lens with iPhone since it can’t be recorded on headset. pic.twitter.com/oF1J9tBTd8
— Justin Ryan (@justinryanio) August 29, 2026





There were a few replays that were particularly impressive, including Ben Rice’s first-inning double that made it feel like I was practically playing left field. I was so close to the action that I could hear muffled chatter in the dugout and see sunflowseeds spit in my direction.
Between innings was particularly magical. There were no commercials, so the view stayed in the stadium, with the camera shifting to the broadcast booth above home plate numerous times to get an expansive overhead view of the whole field. And when David Bednar came in to close the ninth inning, the camera view shifted to center field so I could see his full bullpen entrance and watch him jog to the pitcher’s mound while his walkout song, Styx’s “Renegade,” played in the stadium.
It was so enthralling, I wanted a way to mute the broadcast to soak in the sounds of the stadium. It wasn’t so much that the announcers were bad (though Apple TV has never been known for its broadcast crew), but the Spatial Audio microphones were so clear that the ambiance of the ballpark was enough.
Unfortunately, the game ended 1-0, so there wasn’t a ton of action other than a solo home run, but one particular play stands out as a showcase for what the immersive broadcast brings. In the top of the 7th inning, the Red Sox loaded the bases with one out, so I strapped on my Vision Pro to watch the rest of the inning.
It only took two pitches to end the Red Sox threat. Wilson Contreras hit a fly ball to left field that was caught by Cody Bellinger, who fired the ball home to get a tagging-up Ceddanne Rafaela and end the inning. Watching the play unfold and turning to watch the throw reach home was incredible and better than any TV broadcast I’ve ever watched.
A near homerun
As we wrote in our review, Vision Pro is a pretty heavy device, so keeping it strapped on for two-plus hours isn’t ideal. I don’t have the Dual Knit Band, which might help, but as it was, I watched the game in spurts. I took it off after the first three innings and then returned to it whenever there was a runner in scoring position.
There’s also the issue of eye strain. I have prescription lenses for the Vision Pro, which could exacerbate the issue, but my eyes quickly get tired when using Vision Pro. This was compounded by the sheer immersiveness of the picture that didn’t give my eyes any time to rest.
But I’m already looking forward to the next game on Friday between the L.A. Angels and Pittsburgh Pirates. It’s a shame Vision Pro is so expensive, because every baseball fan should experience it. Maybe Apple can sell Vision Pro tickets next season and start selling hot dogs at the Apple Store. Learn more about the Apple Vision Pro.

title: Farewell, Tim Cook: An era-defining CEO who hung on too long
content:
Macworld





If Apple CEO Tim Cook retired on his 60th birthday, back in 2020, this article would be considerably easier to write.
We’d start with the phenomenal strides made by the company under his watch: Profit and revenue doubled, the market value lifted from $350 billion to $2 trillion (the first U.S. company to hit that milestone). We could discuss the cultural impact made by the Apple Watch and AirPods, the canny pivot to services, and the regulatory storms navigated with deft tact. Ultimately we would agree that his quieter, more dependable qualities had been sadly underrated in comparison with the flashier genius of Steve Jobs, and bid him farewell with an outpouring of positivity.
But instead Cook stuck around, perhaps influenced, towards the end, by the sound of senior executives stampeding past his office on their way out. The mass exodus was carefully orchestrated, he insisted, knowing that his own departure would only make things look worse. But that departure has now finally arrived, and John Ternus will take the top seat tomorrow.
Those additional six years have made Cook’s corporate eulogy rather more of a challenge. On the product side, there have been groundbreaking and successful launches, but the products that were successful were very rarely groundbreaking, and the ones that were were such a flop that Apple had to fire 100 employees in the Vision Pro team. What was the last truly exciting product of the Cook era? The Apple Watch came out in 2015, the AirPods in 2016 and the iPhone X in 2017. Even the first Apple silicon Macs came out in 2020. It’s cruel in some ways that the iPhone Ultra will arrive a few days after Cook leaves office, but that is typical of the man’s selflessness. He wants to give Ternus a head start.
AI has been a mixed bag, to say the least. In recent months, some analysts (including this one) have started to view Cook’s approach in this area more favorably, but let’s be honest: This was no masterstroke. Like spatial computing, Cook looked on AI as a priority target, and the fact Apple ended up outsourcing much of its AI infrastructure and expertise to Google and OpenAI was the lucky result of internal failure rather than wise strategising. Siri AI is now fit for purpose but plenty of reputational damage was done over the course of years as a result of its previous and scandalously long-running incompetence.
Then there’s the ethical side of things: the criteria by which it will be judged, in Cook’s own words, whether or not he was a good and decent man. There were the questions over employee working conditions in 2021 and the anti-unionization tactics in 2022. Cook’s Apple is loosening its iron grip on the App Store but every concession is given up grudgingly and by the smallest possible increments. Such is the company’s relationship with its developer “partners.”
It’s probably wise, finally, to skip quickly over the divisive optics of Cook’s involvement in President Trump’s second term, other than to mention that this relationship seems likely to dominate his time as executive chairman. So much goodwill has been burned in the past six years that some may view this “promotion” as karma.
A complicated legacy, then, and time to give someone else a turn at the wheel. Someone who focuses more on developing great products and a little less on squeezing the costs and honing the logistics. Someone without the baggage of 15 years in the limelight. Someone who can start afresh in their relationship with employees, developers, and customers, and leave governmental liaison duties to the chairman.
But I don’t want to finish on a negative note. These past 15 years have been a time of unprecedented prosperity for Apple, and I have no doubt that Cook’s time in charge will be remembered by Apple fans with fondness. Thanks, Tim, and good luck in the new job.

title: Ternus takeover won't mean a mass Apple exec exodus
content:
An overblown new report claims that Apple has been carefully orchestrating executive retirements for years to not spook shareholders. There is absolutely nothing to support the premise.


The sun is not setting on every current Apple executive - image credit: Apple.
According to Bloomberg, Cook's retirement is one of very many exits that are being scheduled to avoid the appearance of a mass exodus that Ternus will have to deal with.
This is similar to Bloomberg's previous reporting of multiple people quitting Apple and how the company will struggle without them. So the new report is predicting that Apple will soon be unrecognizable, but of the 11 people on Apple's leadership page, it only actually expects two more to go.

title: New Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 Features Revealed
content:
Bloomberg's Mark Gurman today further outlined what to expect from the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 set to be unveiled on September 9.


While it was initially rumored that Touch ID may be coming to the Apple Watch this year, Gurman reiterated that he does not expect the Series 12 or Ultra 4 to have any major design changes compared to the current Series 11 and Ultra 3 models.

expect a ceramic case option to return for the Apple Watch Series 12. Today, he revealed that Apple has tested both white and dark gray ceramic case options, like those offered for the highest-end Apple Watch Series 3 in 2017.

a band with an embedded health sensor, but Gurman did not mention that.

Instead, he expects more ordinary changes, including faster performance and improvements to health and fitness tracking. The Series 11 and Ultra 3 both have the same S10 chip that was used in the Series 10 and Ultra 2, so the S11 chip or newer should provide the first Apple Watch performance improvements in multiple years.

One new feature in testing allows the heart-rate sensor on the Apple Watch to continuously collect data throughout the day, he said. In his newsletter, he added that Apple is also working on revamping its Health and Fitness apps to show more wellness-related metrics "in a similar fashion to increasingly popular app offerings from Whoop and Oura."

An Apple Watch SE 4 is not expected this year.

continues to develop a blood sugar detection feature with a goal of releasing it by 2030.

title: Don't expect an Apple Pencil for the folding iPhone

"If you see a stylus, they blew it," was a Steve Jobs position on why fingers are the input choice on iPhone. While iPad has Apple Pencil, Apple isn't looking to make one for the iPhone Ultra.

title: Top Stories: Apple's 'Surprise and Shine' Event, Plus New Mac mini and Mac Studio
content:
It turned out to be a big week for Apple news this week, as we not only got an official announcement about the upcoming iPhone event but also several hardware announcements including updated Mac mini and Mac Studio models.


Anticipation continues to build for Apple's first foldable iPhone coming at next month's event, while subscribers to the Apple TV streaming service are getting hit with another price increase, so read on below for all of the details.

Top Stories

Apple Event Announced for September 9: 'Surprise and Shine'

Apple this week announced that it plans to hold its annual iPhone-centric event on Wednesday, September 9, at the Apple Park campus in Cupertino, California. The event will begin at 10:00 a.m. Pacific Time, with select members of the media invited to attend.


The September 2026 iPhone event comes with the tagline "Surprise and Shine" and should see Apple announce the iPhone 18 Pro, the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max, and the foldable iPhone, which could be called the iPhone Ultra. There won't be an iPhone 18 this year because Apple is waiting until spring 2027 to launch the more affordable models.

Apple Announces New Mac Mini With M6 and M5 Pro Chips and More

Apple this week announced the next-generation Mac mini, which can be configured with an all-new M6 chip or the M5 Pro chip released earlier this year.


The M6 chip is equipped with a 12-core CPU and a 12-core GPU, up from a 10-core CPU and 10-core GPU in the M5 chip. In addition, the M6 chip features the first-ever dual Neural Engine with two 16-core engines, up from one in previous chips. The M6 chip has up to 170GB/s memory bandwidth, up from 153GB/s for the M5 chip.

Apple said the Mac mini with the M6 chip delivers up to 40% faster CPU performance, up to 4× faster performance for AI tasks in particular, up to 2× faster graphics performance, and up to 2× faster storage speeds compared to the previous-generation model with the 10-core M4 chip, 32GB of unified memory, and 2TB of storage.

Apple Unveils New Mac Studio With M5 Max and M5 Ultra Chips

Alongside the updated Mac mini, Apple also announced new Mac Studio models with the M5 Max and M5 Ultra chips, the latter of which is the company's most powerful chip ever.


The new ‌Mac Studio‌ features a next-generation SSD architecture built on PCIe Gen 6 that Apple says is up to twice as fast as before. The machine also gains Thunderbolt 5 ports with up to 120Gb/s of bandwidth, along with Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 for the first time via Apple's N1 chip. The new ‌Mac Studio‌ also supports genlock over USB-C and can drive up to eight displays.

The M5 Ultra chip includes an up to 36-core CPU that contains 12 super cores and 24 performance cores. It delivers up to 1.25x higher single-threaded performance and up to 1.3x higher multithreaded performance than the M3 Ultra from the previous generation ‌Mac Studio‌.

Apple Releases New Polishing Cloth

Apple this week also updated one of its most meme-worthy products in recent years, with a new version of its Polishing Cloth. It might be just a hint softer and thinner, and it's priced at just $9, half the price of the original one.


Most of Apple's Magic Keyboards for Mac also got updates for the U.S. English versions this week, replacing text labels on edge keys like tab, caps lock, shift, return, and more with glyphs.

Gurman: iPhone Ultra Wows Early Testers, Except for Its Camera

Apple's upcoming foldable "iPhone Ultra" is winning over the few people who have had hands-on time with the device, though the camera setup may leave some users wanting, according to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman.


Writing in his latest "Power On" newsletter, Gurman says people who have used the device – which is reportedly referred to internally as the iPhone Ultra – like how it fits in your pocket, as well as the feel and durability of its hinge mechanism. Testers have also apparently praised the new iPad-like app layouts that take advantage of the larger internal display when the phone is unfolded.

Beyond productivity, video, and gaming, Gurman says Apple's foldable device also performs well as a camera viewfinder. However, the device lacks a telephoto lens, which could cost Apple some sales given the expected price.

Apple TV Streaming Service Receives Price Increase

For the fourth time since its launch, Apple has increased the price of its Apple TV streaming service in the United States, raising monthly pricing by $2 and annual pricing by $20  starting today. As a result of the Apple TV price increase, the Apple One Individual bundle has also gone up in price.



Apple TV (Monthly): $14.99 per month (up from $12.99 per month)

Apple TV (Annually): $119 per year (up from $99 per year)

Apple One (Individual): $21.95 per month (up from $19.95 per month)
Apple TV also received a price increase in Brazil, Chile, and Mexico today, according to Apple, but no other countries are affected in this round of increases.

title: Asahi Linux nears M3 support release, M4 and M5 are on the way
content:
The Asahi Linux project is very close to finally releasing a version with support for M3 Apple Silicon. However, M4 and M5 support is still in development.


Asahi Linux works on earlier Macs. Support for newer models is being worked on. 
Asahi Linux is a project to bring Linux to Apple Silicon, so it can run natively on Apple's ARM-based chips. While the project's progress has been quite gradual in its progression, it is close to reaching a milestone release.
In a project blog post from August 26, the work on supporting M3-series Apple Silicon has gone through a lot of change. While it was shown to be running back in January, albeit in semi-working form, it's in a much better position now.

title: Steve Jobs' 8th Grade Science Project Sells for $34,375
content:
A science project that Apple co-founder Steve Jobs built for his 8th-grade science fair sold at auction for $34,375.


Jobs was attending Cupertino Jr. High when he designed the project, which is titled "What is the SCR?" The lot includes a display board built from plywood with three explanatory panels and a 10-page report with the same title.

The left panel has a wooden model of a "typical silicon-controlled rectifier with its four alternate layers of P- and N-Type semiconductor material," while the center test circuits demonstrate the basic principles and characteristics of the silicon-controlled rectifier, as well as how it is most widely used. The right panel has a diagram and description of a 25-amp silicon-controlled rectifier.

The project is labeled with Jobs' name, and the accompanying report is titled "What is the Silicon-Controlled Rectifier by Steve Jobs, Science, Mrs. Yakel, Feb. 29, 1968."

A note included on the project instructs judges to plug in Circuit II and the oscilloscope to see it operate, and it asks them to "please unplug!" the device after testing it.

Jobs' science fair project came from John Chovanec, Jobs' stepbrother. Chovanec's mother, Marilyn, married Paul Jobs in 1990 and continued to live in the Jobs family home in Los Altos. After Paul Jobs died in 1993, Steve Jobs declined to collect some of his personal belongings that remained in the home. Chovanec apparently asked Jobs to collect the items several times and at one point said he would keep the items himself instead. "Fine, but I don't want to be bothered about it again," Jobs reportedly responded.

sold other items from Jobs' early years, including posters, magazines, bow ties, a desk, and more. A 1977 Apple Computer poster sold for $659,900, while an Apple–1 Byte Shop wooden case owned by Jobs sold for $254,375. The bow ties sold for $113,580.

title: Which Macs Will Get an M6 Chip and Which Won't?
content:
Apple announced new Mac mini machines this week, and the lower-end models include the first M6 chip. The M6 era will be a little complicated, because few Macs are going to get it. We won't have M6 Pro or M6 Max chips, which shakes up the Mac lineup for the next couple of years.

Subscribe to the MacRumors YouTube channel for more videos.

Devices With M6

The ‌Mac mini‌ is the first Mac with an M6, but the chip is going to come to a couple of other products in the lineup.

 	
MacBook Pro - The 14-inch entry-level MacBook Pro could be updated with an M6 chip in October 2026.

 	
iMac - The 24-inch iMac is also expected to get the M6 chip, likely around the time the ‌MacBook Pro‌ is updated.

MacBook Air - The MacBook Air could get the M6 chip in early 2027.

 	
iPad Pro - The next iPad Pro could get the M6 chip.

 	
iPad Air - A future version of the iPad Air is likely to adopt the M6. Apple usually keeps the ‌iPad Air‌ processor one generation behind the ‌iPad Pro‌.


M6 Pro and M6 Max

Apple isn't going to make M6 Pro or M6 Max chips, according to Bloomberg, so the M6 will be the first standalone Apple silicon chip that won't have more powerful variants.

Instead of manufacturing M6 Pro and M6 Max chips, Apple is speeding up its chip development timeline to bring the M7 Pro and M7 Max to market more quickly. The M7 Pro and M7 Max will have technologies that support on-device AI and GPU-intensive software, so they better meet growing demand for processors with those capabilities.
M5 Makes Up the Gap

Macs that would have used an M6 Pro or M6 Max chip are going to be stuck with the M5 Pro and M5 Max until the M7 family is ready. That means the high-end OLED "MacBook Ultra" we're expecting in late 2026 or early 2027 is going to use the same M5 Pro and M5 Max chips that are in the current ‌MacBook Pro‌ models. It's also possible it will get the M5 Ultra.

Mac Studio announced alongside the ‌Mac mini‌ uses M5 Max and M5 Ultra chips.
Short Life Span

The M6 isn't going to be around for long, because Apple plans to launch the M7 in the first half of 2027. The M7 Pro and M7 Max will follow at the end of the year.
M6 Features

The M6 is Apple's first chip built on a new 2-nanometer process that increases transistor density on a smaller die. The process change improves performance and efficiency.

It has a 12-core CPU with what Apple says is the world's fastest CPU core, a larger 12-core GPU with Neural Accelerators for each core, a new Dual 16-core Neural Engine, and up to 170GB/s memory bandwidth.

title: Apple's Siri Settlement: Here's When iPhone Owners Can Submit Claims
content:
In May, Apple agreed to pay $250 million to settle a U.S. class action lawsuit over Siri AI's delayed launch, and eligible iPhone users could receive up to a $95 payout. Today, a new court document revealed when customers will likely be able to begin submitting claims.


If the dates proposed by Apple's lawyers are approved by the judge, eligible customers would begin to be notified about the settlement on Monday, September 21 this year, and claim submissions would likely begin around that date. The claims period would end on Monday, December 21, giving customers around 90 days to take action.

Earlier this month, the judge set the final approval hearing for February 24, 2027, so payments to customers are not expected to begin until next year. For now, no action is required from customers, as the settlement website with a claims form has yet to go live. We will continue to provide updates on the case as they become available.

Below, we have answered some key questions regarding the lawsuit.

Why Was Apple Sued?

In June 2024, Apple previewed new Siri capabilities powered by Apple Intelligence, including understanding of a user's personal context, on-screen awareness, and deeper per-app controls. For example, Apple showed an iPhone user asking Siri about their mother's flight and lunch reservation plans based on info from the Mail and Messages apps.

in a TV commercial starring actor Bella Ramsey, and elsewhere.


In March 2025, Apple delayed the launch of the personalized version of Siri, leading to the company being hit with a class action lawsuit alleging false advertising.

In a statement, Apple touted a range of other Apple Intelligence features it had already released. Nevertheless, Apple agreed to settle the lawsuit "to stay focused" on "delivering the most innovative products and services to our users."

finally announced "Siri AI" at WWDC 2026 in June, and the revamped assistant is available to test on the iOS 27 beta ahead of a September release.


Am I Eligible?

To be eligible to submit a claim, you must reside in the U.S. and have purchased any iPhone 15 Pro or iPhone 16 model between June 10, 2024 and March 29, 2025.

It is unlikely that individuals who submit a claim will still need to have physical possession of an eligible iPhone model. However, there is a possibility that proof of purchase or other information will be required, such as the device's serial number. Exact requirements will be outlined on the settlement website, which is still not live.

How Much Will Apple Pay Me?

According to the terms of the settlement, each person who files an eligible claim will receive a per-device payment of $25, but this amount could increase up to $95 if the total number of claims submitted is lower than anticipated.

Where and When Can I Submit a Claim?

Later this year, a settlement website is expected to go live with an online claims form.

title: iPhone 18 Pro: Release date, price, specs and latest rumors ahead of Apple’s event
content:
Macworld





The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are expected to launch at an Apple event on September 9, 2026 featuring several cutting-edge hardware advancements, including the debut of Apple’s C2 modem, and a shift to a 2nm manufacturing process for the A20 Pro chip. 
Other key rumored upgrades include a smaller Dynamic Island with under-display Face ID components and camera improvements that may include variable aperture on the Pro Max and enhanced sensors.
Alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max Apple is said to be planning to launch the ultra-premium folding iPhone. However, in a change to the usual schedule, the company is expected to shift the launch of the iPhone 18 spring 2027 to keep the spotlight on the Pro series during its traditional September debut. Here’s a quick summary of what all the rumors and leaks say to expect from the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max in 2026.


What are the biggest upgrades for iPhone 18 Pro & Pro Max
Expected unveiling at Apple’s September 9 event
Smaller Dynamic Island, potentially with some Face ID components under the display
Variable-aperture main camera
A20 Pro chip built on TSMC’s 2nm process
Apple C2 cellular modem
New N2 wireless/networking chip
Larger battery, particularly on the Pro Max
Simplified Camera Control
Revised, more seamless rear Ceramic Shield design
Possible 5G satellite connectivity
Likely price increase due to soaring memory and component costs
How is iPhone 18 Pro/Max different from iPhone 17 Pro/Max?
Split release schedule (Pro first, base later)
Smaller or modified Dynamic Island
Possible under-display Face ID components
New modem (shift away from Qualcomm)
Camera experimentation (rumored variable aperture on Pro Max)


						

							




iPhone 18 Pro/Max vs iPhone 17 Pro/Max

Face IDUnder-displayPossibleNo change since 2022 iPhone 14 Pro

 Comparing iPhone 18 Pro rumors to current iPhone 17 Pro






When will the new iPhones launch?
Apple has confirmed that it will hold an event on Wednesday September 9, 2026 and it is highly likely that new iPhones will launch at that event.
However, multiple reports suggest Apple could significantly change its release strategy that year. Rather than launching the entire iPhone 18 lineup at once, Apple is reportedly planning to release only its premium models in September 2026: the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and a new foldable iPhone are widely expected to headline the event.
According to these reports, the standard iPhone 18 and iPhone 18e and a second generation iPhone Air will follow in spring 2027. If accurate, this would mark the biggest change to Apple’s iPhone launch schedule since the lineup expanded beyond a single annual release.
A staggered rollout would allow Apple to focus attention on its highest-end devices during the holiday shopping season while giving the company a second major iPhone launch window in the first half of 2027. It would also mean that every new iPhone introduced in September 2026 would likely start at $999 or more.
As always, Apple has not confirmed these plans, and the release schedule could change before launch.
During Apple’s Q3 earnings call, Apple CEO Tim Cook warned that “the impact from the supply constraints (will) increase significantly.” That means supplies of new products, such as the iPhone 18 Pro, could be severely limited at launch. It may take longer than usual for orders to be fulfilled.

 The anticipated launch dates for the 2026-2027 iPhones






What will the iPhone 18 Pro/Max look like and what are the color choices?
The design of the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max is said to resemble the iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max, but some changes are predicted.
One possible change, shared by a Weibo leaker in September 2025, is a “slightly transparent” ceramic shield section on the back of Pro models. This glass/Ceramic Shield area around MagSafe is now rumored to become more frosted and visually seamless. 
Macworld contributor Filipe Esposito reported that a trusted source had revealed one of the new colorways for the iPhone 18 Pro to be Dark Cherry, replacing the iPhone 17 Pro’s Cosmic Orange option.
Recent rumors claimed that the new phones will be significantly thicker than previous models, but all the evidence we have seen says that’s not the case. Instead, we expect the body to have about the same thickness as the iPhone 17 Pro/Max but with a thicker camera bump area.
Another report suggests that the Camera Control on the side of the iPhone will be pressure sensing instead of a touch-sensing layer. This redesign is said to be aimed at reducing the cost and complexity.  
A recent ransomware attack against an Apple parts supplier included images from an iPhone 18 Pro “drop test” and other parts, and they corroborate prior rumors about the overall shape and design of the phone, which is broadly the same as the iPhone 17 Pro.
Other shades are said to include: Light Blue, Dark Gray, and Silver. There was also a coffee shade rumored (via Digital Chat Station).

iPhone 18 Pro colors revealed! #iphone #apple

As with the iPhone 17 Pro, there will be no black option, according to Instant Digital.
Screen sizes are expected to remain at 6.3 and 6.9 inches. The Pro models will also retain the wider three-camera raised plateau.
Most likely: Design changes will be minimal, with the biggest visible differences limited to colors and subtle refinements.


						

							


What’s new with the iPhone 18 Pro/Max camera?

				
					

				
			
Eugen Wegmann




Apple may introduce variable aperture technology to the 48MP main camera on the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max (potentially only the Pro Max), allowing mechanical control over light intake and depth of field. This has long been a perk limited to high-end professional cameras.
If the rumor (from Digital Chat Station on Weibo) is true, iPhone users will be able to mechanically control how much light reaches the sensor for the first time, allowing more control over depth of field and sharpness. This could elevate portrait shots by improving the applied depth of field effect, as well as minimizing overexposure.
Wider telephoto apertures on the Pro models should also result in better low-light performance.
For some time (since January 2025) Samsung has been said to be working on a new three-layer stacked camera sensor called ‘PD-TR-Logic,’ and this could appear in the iPhone 18 series. This image sensor is expected to enhance the camera’s responsiveness, while also offering advantages such as reduced photo noise, improved dynamic range. The main Wide camera sensor is expected to be larger than usual, which offers many benefits.
The front-facing camera may also get an upgrade beyond the rumored changes to the housing (as discussed elsewhere the selfie camera may be housed in a smaller hole-punch cut out, reducing the size of the Dynamic Island). The iPhone 17 generation features 18MP sensors for the selfie camera, but this may increase to 24MP in the next generation, according to leaker WhyLab on Weibo.
More megapixels would lead to improved video calls and better low-light performance. 
Most likely: Incremental improvements, with a new variable aperture feature on the Pro Max.


						

							


Will the iPhone 18 Pro/Max Dynamic Island or front camera change?

				
					

				
			
Britta O’Boyle




Apple hasn’t changed the Dynamic Island since the iPhone 14 Pro, but the iPhone 18 Pro may introduce some adjustments.
Some reports suggest Face ID components could move under the display, shrinking the Dynamic Island. 
A report in December 2025 from Weibo account “Smart Pikachu” claimed that Apple is testing an under-display “micro-transparent glass panel” for some Face ID sensors. This should enable a smaller Dynamic Island for iPhone 18 Pro. 
The ever-reliable Mark Gurman at Bloomberg also reported that Apple will “shrink” the Dynamic Island on the iPhone 18 models, so there’s strong evidence that some of the several sensors and emitters required for Face ID will be under the display or combined.
A spy shot published in March by noted leaker IceUniverse on X gives us a view of how much smaller the Dynamic Island could be.

				
					

				
			
IceUniverse/X




There have been conflicting claims that the position of the front-facing camera may also change: 
In December 2025 The Information claimed Apple will put the Face ID sensors under the display, and move the front camera to the upper left corner in a punch-hole design. This would make the iPhone 18 Pro/ Max the first iPhones with a front camera in the corner.
However, Prominent leaker account Instant Digital said on Weibo in January 2026 that front camera claim was based on a mistranslation, and only the infrared sensor moves under the display. Leakers ShrimpApplePro and Ross Young of DSCC corroborated Instant Digital’s claims.
Most likely: A smaller Dynamic Island with some components of Face ID under the glass. Smaller pill cut out for camera, remaining in central position.


						

							


Will the iPhone 18 Pro/Max display change?

				
					

				
			
Stephan Wiesend




Screen sizes should be consistent with the 6.3 and 6.9-inch displays on the current models, but reports suggest a massive jump in brightness from the current 1600 nits HDR and 3,000 nits peak. 
According to Weibo leaker, Instant Digital, Chinese supplier BOE has revealed that Apple is targeting unprecedentedly high brightness requirements for the display. The Elec corroborated this, claiming BOE is struggling with iPhone OLED production so panel orders have been shifted to Samsung Display.
Most likely: An increase in brightness is expected, but there are no details yet on the extent of the improvement.


						

							


How powerful will the A20 chip in the iPhone 18 Pro/Max be?
The iPhone 18 series is expected to use a new A20 chip, built on TSMC’s N2 (2nm) process. This will represent a major architectural shift for Apple’s smartphone silicon, primarily due to the transition to a more advanced manufacturing process. 
This move to a smaller process allows for more transistors in the same space, which is projected to deliver up to 15% faster performance and 30% better power efficiency compared to the A19 chip. 
The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max models will utilize an A20 Pro variant to further differentiate their capabilities. This increased power is expected to support advanced features.
The A20 could also follow the lead of Apple’s M-series chips by introducing “super cores,” similar to the M5 chip 
The A20 is rumored to use a new process called Wafer-Level Multi-Chip Module (WMCM) packaging to incorporate the RAM into the SoC’s package. It’s not clear what the benefit will be, but more tightly integrated RAM can mean more memory bandwidth and lower RAM latency, or better power efficiency.
Most likely: A typical Apple leap in efficiency and speed, with behind-the-scenes gains rather than dramatic user-visible changes.


						

							


Will iPhone 18 Pro/Max battery life improve?
Apple works to make battery life as long as possible every year, especially in the Pro model iPhones. 
A July report claimed that the battery capacity of the iPhone 18 Pro Max will have a battery capacity of 5,235 mAh on the Nano SIM model and 5,425 mAh on the eSIM-only version. That’s about 6-8% more capacity than the current model. Further reports have puts the U.S. eSIM iPhone 18 Pro Max at 5,567mAh. 
The “Pro Max” variant of the iPhone gets a higher-capacity battery nearly every year, usually a couple hundred mAh more, thanks to better internal design and improving battery chemistry and manufacturing techniques. But battery life is a function of more than just battery capacity—the power use of the processor, display, and wireless radios all play an important point.
We think it’s likely the iPhone 18 Pro/Max will have higher-capacity batteries, and battery life at least as long as the iPhone 17 Pro/Max. But a significantly longer battery life is hard to predict.


						

							


Will connectivity improve (5G, Wi-Fi, satellite) with iPhone 18 Pro/Max?
iPhone 18 Pro models are rumored to feature the second generation of Apple’s in-house 5G modem, the C2 chip. 
The C2 modem, which hasn’t yet launched, is expected to replace Qualcomm across Apple’s lineup. This should improve:
Efficiency
Performance
mmWave support
There are also reports that the new iPhone will gain full satellite internet support, expanding beyond emergency use. In October 2025, The Information claimed that Apple is gearing up to support 5G networks that are served from satellites. 
While the iPhone has offered satellite connectivity for emergency situations for years, if this rumor is true it would allow the iPhone 18 models to have full internet access via satellite, not just emergency services.
As of April 2026, it looks like Apple is teaming up with Amazon to provide this service. Early in April, Amazon announced that it has acquired Globalstar, who was the provider of iPhone and Apple Watch satellite connectivity. So now iPhones and Apple Watches will now fall under Amazon Leo, Amazon’s satellite internet network.
The Wi-Fi/Bluetooth chip (N1) will likely remain unchanged. Apple debuted its local networking chip in the iPhone 17 line – the N1 supports Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread networking. We haven’t heard anything about an N2, and honestly, one probably isn’t needed so soon. Could Apple have an “N1X” surprise in store the way it did with the C1X? It’s possible, but so far the rumor mill expects Apple to build the iPhone 18 line with the same N1 chip as found in the iPhone 17.
Most likely: A meaningful upgrade in connectivity, especially if satellite internet expands.


						

							


How much will the iPhone 18 Pro/Max cost?
With Apple increasing prices for Macs and iPads in June due to high memory and chip costs there are expectations that the iPhones introduced in 2026 will also see a price hike. 
Indeed, on August 24 Mark Gurman reported that an iPhone price increase appears inevitable because of those higher component costs.
IDC has suggested increases of up to $200 for the Pro models, while analyst Jeff Pu has indicated prices could rise by as much as $250-$300.
The introduction of a folding iPhone could also dramatically change the pricing structure, as it will reportedly have a starting price of $1,999 or more.

It’s said that by putting some of the Face ID technology under the display Apple will be able to shrink the size of the Dynamic Island.

title: Anker’s powerhouse 250W desktop charger just hit a new record low
content:
Macworld





		
Anker Prime 6-port Charging Station
View Deal
If you have entirely too many charging bricks on your desk, you absolutely need a charging station. This Anker 250W charging station has six ports, and they’re all ready to handle your laptop, smartphone, tablets, and whatever else you need to charge. It’s only $95 at Amazon right now after a 37 percent discount, the best price we’ve seen for this model.
Despite its small footprint, this charging station is an absolute beast that can deliver a full 250W of power across all six ports. The lead USB-C port alone can push up to 140W, so it charges a laptop as fast as the wall adapter would. It can take your 16-inch MacBook Pro to 50 percent in just 25 minutes, Anker says, which is quite impressive.
The station features four USB-C ports on the front and a couple of USB-A on the side. There’s also a smart control dial that lets you shift power on the fly, giving priority to whatever needs it most in the moment. You can see exactly how much power is being pushed through each port on the built-in 2.26-inch LCD display.
You do have to keep in mind that if all ports are in use, then the left-most C-port will only deliver 100W of power, while the rest of the USB-C ports cap at 45W and the USB-A top out at 15W.
For $95 at an all-time low, this is a smart way to power your entire desk from one tidy hub.

title: The MacRumors Show: Apple's Surprisingly Big Week of Announcements
content:
It's been an unusually big week for Apple announcements. On this week's episode of The MacRumors Show, we discuss the new Mac mini and Mac Studio, the M6 and M5 Ultra chips, and invites to Apple's September event. 

Subscribe to The MacRumors Show YouTube channel for more videos

Apple confirmed on Wednesday that its annual iPhone event will take place on Wednesday, September 9 at Apple Park, starting at 10:00 a.m. Pacific Time, with select members of the media invited to attend. The event's tagline is "Surprise and Shine." Apple is expected to introduce at least six new products, including the the Apple Watch Series 12, Apple Watch Ultra 4, iPhone 18 Pro, ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max, and the first foldable iPhone. Pre-orders should follow shortly after, and along with release dates for iOS 27, iPadOS 27 and macOS 27 Golden Gate.

announced the new Mac mini on Tuesday, offering M6 and M5 Pro chip options. The machine gains an N1 networking chip, bringing Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, and moves to 2.5Gb Ethernet as standard, up from 1Gb, with a 10Gb option. Thunderbolt 5 is restricted to the M5 Pro model, which gets three Thunderbolt 5 ports while the M6 model keeps Thunderbolt 4. Genlock support over USB-C also helps to sync a display's refresh timing to a camera such as the iPhone 17 Pro. Pricing starts at $899 with 16GB and 256GB, rising to $1,699 for the M5 Pro at 24GB and 512GB. Pre-orders are now open, with launch on September 22. 

first 2nm chip. Its 12-core CPU is split into 2 super cores, 4 performance cores and 6 efficiency cores, making it the first Apple chip to combine all three core types in one design. Super cores are Apple's top tier, optimized for single-threaded speed. The 12-core GPU features a Neural Accelerator in each core for the first time in a ‌Mac mini‌. The GPU also adds an updated shader architecture, Dynamic Caching, and hardware-accelerated ray tracing, while an all-new Dual 16-core Neural Engine doubles peak compute over the previous generation, with system frameworks able to drive both engines at once. Memory starts at 16GB and tops out at 32GB, running at up to 170GB/s. M5 Pro scales further, to an 18-core CPU, a 20-core GPU and up to 64GB at 307GB/s.

new Mac Studio arrived alongside the ‌Mac mini‌, with M5 Max and M5 Ultra chip options. The M5 Max offers an 18-core CPU with 6 super cores and 12 performance cores, an up-to-40-core GPU with Neural Accelerators in every core, and up to 128GB of memory at 614GB/s, with the GPU running up to 50% faster than the previous generation. Both configurations move to a next-generation SSD architecture on PCIe Gen 6 for up to twice the storage performance, and gain up to six Thunderbolt 5 ports at 120Gb/s, and the same genlock support as the ‌Mac mini‌. Apple's N1 chip also brings Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 to the ‌Mac Studio‌. Pricing starts at $2,499 for the M5 Max at 36GB and 512GB, and $5,499 for the M5 Ultra at 96GB and 1TB, with the 512GB memory option not arriving until late October.

first quad-die chip, using a next-generation version of UltraFusion to join two dual-die M5 Max chips into a single processor. The result is a CPU with up to 36 cores, 12 super and 24 performance, delivering 1.25x the single-threaded and 1.3x the multithreaded performance of the M3 Ultra. Its up-to-80-core GPU is the most powerful Apple silicon GPU ever made and the first on an Ultra chip to feature Neural Accelerators. Second-generation Dynamic Caching, hardware-accelerated mesh shading and third-generation ray tracing lift graphics up 40% over the M3 Ultra, and the chip features a 32-core Neural Engine. Memory reaches 512GB at 1.2TB/s, which is a 50% bandwidth increase.

Apple Polishing Cloth at $9, down from $19, and refreshed U.S. Magic Keyboards for the Mac, now featuring glyphs instead of edge text. Apple Support's 1-800-APL-CARE line is also now answered by a generative AI assistant in the U.S. and Canada.
